title: SEED on-policy and hindsight-SFT ablation drops reduce to occupancy matching and cold-start capability
dead_end_scope: The standalone claim that SEED's 7.4-point drop with a static offline skill library or 5.8-point drop without hindsight-skill SFT identifies a new self-evolution mechanism merely from those component ablations.

fresh_phenomenon_closure.closure_scope: the static-offline-skill and no-hindsight-skill-SFT ablation drops only

counter_explanation.statement: SEED's own theory and ablation interpretation supply mature explanations for both drops. Appendix A.1 explicitly motivates on-policy hindsight as an occupancy-matched adaptive target: skills extracted from the current policy's own trajectories track its current state-action occupancy and failure modes, whereas a static offline library can be distribution-mismatched as the policy evolves. The 7.4-point static-library drop is therefore directly expressible by ordinary distribution/occupancy shift and stale-supervision principles. Separately, hindsight-skill SFT is the initialization that teaches the actor/analyzer to perform trajectory analysis before the self-evolving RL stage. Removing it changes cold-start representation/competence, so the 5.8-point drop is predicted by initialization and prerequisite-capability effects unless initial analyzer competence and supervised information are matched. Neither one-factor ablation by itself identifies a new causal primitive of self-evolution.
counter_explanation.opposite_prediction: Holding policy occupancy fixed, guidance derived from a mismatched offline distribution can underperform guidance aligned to current trajectories even without a new mechanism; holding downstream RL fixed, weakening the initial analyzer/actor competence can lower later performance through ordinary initialization and optimization path dependence. Both effects should shrink when occupancy/support and initial competence/supervised information are matched.
counter_explanation.opposite_principle: On-policy skill benefit is first an occupancy-matching problem, while hindsight-SFT benefit is first a cold-start capability problem; component ablation drops are not new self-evolution mechanisms unless those mature sources of advantage are matched and a residual remains.
counter_explanation.opposite_search_seed: For the on-policy claim, compare libraries with matched task/trajectory support, skill quality, size, recency information, and policy occupancy while varying only the mechanism of skill generation; require a held-out residual beyond distribution shift, stale supervision, and support mismatch. For the SFT claim, match initial analyzer/actor trajectory-analysis competence, supervised token/information budget, and downstream RL budget while varying the initialization path; require a residual beyond initialization and optimization-path baselines. Do not reopen from another unmatched static-vs-on-policy or with-vs-without-pretraining ablation.
counter_explanation.scope: SEED arXiv:2607.14777, especially Section 4.6 ablations and Appendix A.1/A.3 on occupancy-matched hindsight and analyzer synchronization.
alternative_explanations_ruled_out: The static offline library and on-policy library are distribution-matched treatments: false; the paper explicitly motivates current-policy trajectories as better reflecting evolving behavior/failure modes and develops occupancy-matching theory.

Removing hindsight-skill SFT changes only a label while preserving initial analyzer competence: false; the paper states that SFT equips actor/analyzer with trajectory-analysis capability before subsequent self-evolution.
The ablation drops estimate an interaction unique to self-evolution: false; they are one-factor removals without same-information matching of occupancy or initial capability.
The closure implies SEED is ineffective: false; it closes only standalone novelty claims inferred from these two ablation drops.
counter_explanation.reopen_condition: Reopen the on-policy residual only with occupancy/support/skill-quality/size and information matched between on-policy and offline libraries; reopen the SFT residual only with initial trajectory-analysis competence, supervised information budget, and downstream optimization budget matched. In either case require a repeatable held-out difference beyond distribution shift, stale supervision, cold-start initialization, and optimization-path dependence.

scientific_interpretation.safe_claim: SEED provides evidence that current-policy skills and hindsight-SFT are useful. The cited ablation drops are already predicted by occupancy matching and cold-start capability principles and therefore do not by themselves establish a new self-evolution mechanism.
